title: structured-decoding-contract-layer-and-tokenizer-sanity-checks
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a decoding contract layer that normalizes structured-output constraints across backends, streaming-safe function-call framing, and tokenizer-level sanity checks to reduce broken fragments during streaming. Improves stability for OpenAI compatibility envelopes.
description:
Summary: Introduce a decoding contract layer that sits between the API's structured-output schema and the backend-constrained decoders. This PR consolidates CFG/regex/tokenizer constraint translations into a single, streaming-safe contract, and adds tokenizer-level sanity checks and a frag-join protocol so function/tool calls and structured envelopes survive streaming fragmentation.

Motivation: We see two classes of production failures: 1) backends enforcing grammar/regex constraints fail when tokenizers split tokens mid-pattern (token-boundary splits) causing decoding dead-ends; 2) streaming responses that emit function-call envelopes across chunks lead to parse failures in the OpenAI-compat layer. The decoding contract unifies translation rules and emits a small, backend-agnostic instruction set (contract) that decoders consume. It also defines a minimal streaming framing and a tokenizer sanity pass to detect and repair boundary splits.

Key changes and rationale:
- New module: src/runtime/decoding/contract_layer.rs: implements ContractBuilder, ContractSanitizer, and a lightweight ContractSerializer. ContractBuilder compiles schema/regex/CFG into an intermediate contract representation optimized for streaming checks and prefix-preservation. ContractSanitizer runs a pass over token-boundary slices and emits repair actions (escape, join-hint) when constraints would otherwise deadlock.
- OpenAI compatibility shim updates: packages/openai-compat/src/stream_shim.ts now understands the frag-join protocol and will buffer until a minimal contract-safe unit is available before emitting function_call or tool frames downstream. This reduces inadvertent malformed function_call events visible to customers.
- Tokenizer hooks: sdk/python/redwood/tokenizer/sanity.py adds public utilities used by the SDK and runtime to compute safe split points and re-encode join tokens. This is intentionally language-agnostic and used by both Python and TS SDKs in tests.
- Tests: tests/structured/fragmentation_test.py and tests/structured/contract_serialization_test.py cover edgecases: regex lookahead spanning token boundaries, CFG anchor tokens split mid-utf8, and OpenAI-style function_call spanning stream chunks. A new flaky test was stabilized by adding deterministic seed scheduling in tests/ci/seed_manager.py.
- Docs: docs/structured-output.md describes the contract format and recommended server-side configs for streaming SLOs. Example snippet (contract fragment): "{\"action\":\"allow_prefix\",\"pattern\":\"^\u003canswer\u003e\"}" (stored as newline-delimited json in contract blobs).

Files changed (high level):
- src/runtime/decoding/contract_layer.rs
- src/runtime/decoding/contract_cache.rs
- packages/openai-compat/src/stream_shim.ts

Small illustrative snippet (contract sanitizer logic, simplified): "if pattern_crosses_token_boundary(pattern, tokens) { emit_repair_action(join_hint) } else { allow_prefix(match_len) }"

Bench and behavioral results:
- Local benchmarks (stress-1k sim streams) show a 4.5x reduction in parse-errors attributable to tokenizer fragmentation for constrained decoding workloads.
- Latency impact: contract translation adds ~0.6-1.2ms p99 on the server-side during cold contract compile; cached contract path is negligible.
- Memory: contract cache + sanitizer adds ~1.6MB per contract shard.

Backwards compatibility and migration:
- Contracts are emitted when a model route has structured_output schema present. Existing routes without structured_output are unaffected.
- The OpenAI-compat shim falls back to previous behavior if the remote peer doesn't support streaming fragments (controlled via compatibility flag).

Review thread (highlights):
- Amit Patel (reviewer): "Can we avoid adding additional heap allocations in the hot path? The contract serializer may be called per-request on rare routes." Author reply (Maya): "Good point. I added a contract_cache with a thin Arc-backed read path and added microbenchmarks; updated code swaps to zero-copy slices for serialized blobs. See contract_cache.rs."
- Lena Ortiz: "Tests look good but please add an integration test that runs with the dedicated runtime on amd64 with the 8k tokenizer to catch BPE edgecases." Author: "Added fragmentation_test that runs parameterized tokenizers; marked slow by default and included in nightly CI."
- Karan Singh: "OpenAI-compat changes look safe but ensure we don't buffer arbitrarily and break SLOs." Author: "The frag-join protocol includes a per-route max-buffer-bytes and emits partial-allowed tokens as a graceful degradation; documented defaults are 256 bytes for consumer routes."

CI history:
- Initial run: lint and unit tests passed; two flaky fragmentation tests failed intermittently (seed scheduling uncovered race).
- Second run: after fixing seed_manager and seeding deterministic RNG, all tests passed.
- Integration job (dedicated runtime amd64) passed in nightly.

Merge notes:
- Squash merge with release note entry.
- Rollout plan: staged for hosted API routes with structured_output enabled first, monitor parse-errors and stream error rates.
